name: Roey Lalazar
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Wonderful (enterprise AI agent platform)
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded Wonderful in early 2025 with CEO Bar Winkler. Wonderful builds AI agents and an 'AI operating system' for enterprise customer service and back-office workflows, focusing on non-English markets. It raised $150M at a $2B valuation (Series B, 2026), then $550M at ~$5B in September 2026, and has ~650 staff.
interesting_fact: Wonderful planned to grow from 350 to ~900 employees in a single year to serve enterprises in 30+ countries across Europe, the Middle East, APAC and Latin America, pairing its AI agents with local deployment teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wonderful, Lalazar founded Kaps, an AI-based localization platform. That language work foreshadows Wonderful's focus on non-English-speaking markets.
notes: Low personal media profile; CEO Bar Winkler does most of the press. Hurun's $2B valuation is outdated (now ~$5B). Some outlets misspell his name as 'Lalzar'/'Royel'.

name: Venkata Sanjayreddy Gunupati
current_role: Vice Chairman, GVK Group (Hyderabad); founder of GVK Biosciences, now Aragen Life Sciences (stepped off the Aragen board in Jan 2023)
profile: Better known as G V Sanjay Reddy, son of GVK Group founder G V Krishna Reddy. He set up GVK BIO in Hyderabad in 2001 as an informatics company. It grew into Aragen Life Sciences, a contract research and manufacturing firm with 2,800+ scientists and 450+ clients, renamed in 2021. He also led the family's infrastructure businesses, including the Mumbai airport.
interesting_fact: Aragen, which he founded as GVK BIO in 2001, now serves 7 of the 10 largest pharma companies and 100+ biotechs, and has one of India's largest pools of chemists.
deep_cut_fact: The University of Michigan's Ross School of Business invited GV Sanjay Reddy to address its graduating class. The GVK Group's CSR arm, GVK EMRI, runs '108' emergency ambulance services in more than 15 Indian states.
notes: Name as filed in Indian corporate records is 'Venkata Sanjayreddy Gunupati'. Registry aggregators show he ceased as an Aragen director on 31 Jan 2023. The Ross page is behind a bot wall, so only its title was verified (via a Wikipedia GVK EMRI citation). Web-search quota was exhausted mid-lane.

name: Matthias Jungblut
profile: German software entrepreneur who co-founded osapiens in 2018 with Alberto Zamora and Stefan Wawrzinek after the three met at SAP. osapiens' cloud 'HUB' handles supply-chain transparency, ESG/regulatory compliance and carbon data for 2,500+ companies. In January 2026 it reached a $1B+ valuation with a $100M round from Decarbonization Partners (BlackRock/Temasek), after Goldman Sachs invested in 2024.
interesting_fact: osapiens became Germany's first unicorn of 2026; Jungblut told Handelsblatt the new investors 'can open doors for us' for planned US and Asia expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Jungblut champions Mannheim over Berlin or Munich. The founders deliberately chose a site 30 km from SAP's Walldorf HQ: 'Mannheim is a good location that is underestimated... very good colleges and universities in Mannheim, Karlsruhe, and Darmstadt.'
notes: He and Zamora are the public faces of osapiens and often quoted in German business press (Handelsblatt, FAZ). The founders previously sold a supply-chain monitoring company to Honeywell (per GTAI).
